html:
SMTO-TSK-0026 — SMTO is already running as many tasks as it can

GUID: 1b6d7b0b-231a-4bc5-ab47-2d2f6ffdd59d
Slug: task-capacity-unavailable
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • SMTO is already working on the most tasks it is allowed to run at the same time, so it didn't start this one. Tasks that are already running keep going.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look through your open conversations for tasks that are still running. Wait for one to finish, or select Stop on a task you no longer need. Each task that finishes or stops frees a slot for new work.
  2. Before sending again, check the conversation to see whether your message already started as a task. This avoids running the same work twice if it was accepted after all.
  3. If a task is still running in this conversation, send your message with Queue so it starts automatically when that task finishes. Queued messages wait for a free slot instead of being turned away.
  4. If you often need more tasks at once, ask the person who manages SMTO to raise Settings › Operate › Execution › Parallel run limit (the maximum is 8). This setting decides how many tasks SMTO runs at the same time.

What success looks like

  • Your message starts running, or it appears in the Queued list and starts when another task finishes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with how many tasks were running. Don't keep resending the same message quickly; that can start duplicate work as soon as a slot opens.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Task admission found no free run slot (the Parallel run limit is reached, or eight live execution owners exist), so a non-queued request, a failed-task retry or a workflow Run now was refused.

What this means

  • The current available-run-slot calculation is zero or less when a new non-durable task, retry or recipe invocation requests admission. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • The current available-run-slot calculation is zero or less when a new non-durable task, retry or recipe invocation requests admission.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect accepted active tasks and durable queue state before submitting another copy.

How to fix it

  • Compare active runs with agent_parallel_run_limit (Settings › Operate › Execution › Parallel run limit, 1–8) and the fixed ceiling of eight live execution owners in native_run_owners. Submit through the conversation task queue so the request waits for a slot, or retry once a run finishes; first confirm the earlier submission was not already accepted.
  • Queue the prompt as a durable task or wait for an active task to finish. Reconnect to an already accepted task instead of submitting the same work again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Capacity becomes available and the intended task is admitted once through its normal queue/control path.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
